## Proof

**Setup.** The matrix is
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&u'\\ v&I\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb K^{m\times m},
\]
where $u,v\in\mathbb K^{m-1}$. Only the first row ($u'$) and first column ($v$) are "dense"; the trailing $(m{-}1)\times(m{-}1)$ block is the identity.

---

### The permutation

Let $P$ be the permutation that sends the index ordering $(1,2,\dots,m)$ to $(2,3,\dots,m,1)$, i.e. it moves the first index to the last position. Applying $P$ to both rows and columns gives
\[
\tilde A \;=\; PAP' \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} I & v\\[2pt] u' & 1\end{pmatrix},
\]
where $I$ is the $(m{-}1)\times(m{-}1)$ identity. (The top-left block is the $(2,\dots,m)\times(2,\dots,m)$ submatrix of $A$, which is $I$; the top-right is $v$; the bottom-left is $u'$; the bottom-right is $A_{11}=1$.)

---

### LU decomposition of $\tilde A$

We perform Gaussian elimination on $\tilde A$ using the natural ordering (rows $1,\dots,m$).

**Steps $1,\dots,m{-}1$.** At step $k$ the pivot is $\tilde A_{kk}=1$ (a diagonal entry of the identity block $I$). The only row below the pivot with a nonzero entry in column $k$ is the last row (row $m$), where the entry is $u_k$. The multiplier is $\ell_{mk}=u_k/1=u_k$. We subtract $u_k\times\text{row }k$ from row $m$. Since row $k$ is $e_k$ with $v_k$ appended, this zeroes out $\tilde A_{mk}$ and updates the last entry of row $m$ by $-u_k v_k$.

After all $m{-}1$ steps the last entry of row $m$ becomes
\[
1-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}u_k v_k \;=\; 1-u'v.
\]

No fill-in occurs in the identity block (it is already upper triangular), and the only off-diagonal modifications are confined to the last row of $L$ and the last column of $U$.

**Result.** The factors are
\[
\boxed{L=\begin{pmatrix} I & 0\\[2pt] u' & 1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
U=\begin{pmatrix} I & v\\[2pt] 0 & 1-u'v\end{pmatrix}.}
\]

**Verification.**
\[
LU=\begin{pmatrix} I&0\\ u'&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} I&v\\ 0&1-u'v\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix} I&v\\ u'&u'v+1-u'v\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix} I&v\\ u'&1\end{pmatrix}=\tilde A.\;\checkmark
\]

(The decomposition requires $1-u'v\neq 0$; this is also $\det\tilde A=\det A\neq 0$, i.e. $A$ nonsingular, which is the standard condition for LU to exist without pivoting.)

---

### Why storage grows linearly

The factors have the following **non-structural** (data-carrying) entries:

| Factor | Non-structural content | Storage |
|--------|----------------------|---------|
| $L$ | the row vector $u'$ (last row, $m{-}1$ entries) | $m-1$ |
| $U$ | the column vector $v$ (last column, $m{-}1$ entries) and the scalar $1-u'v$ | $m$ |

Everything else is **structural**: the identity blocks $I$, the zero blocks $0$, and the unit diagonal of $L$ are known a priori and need not be stored. Hence the total storage for the pair $(L,U)$ is
\[
(m-1)+m \;=\; 2m-1 \;=\; O(m).
\]

**Contrast with the unpermuted case.** Without permutation, the first pivot is $1$, the first column of $L$ is $(1,v')'$ (cost $O(m)$, fine), but the Schur complement is
\[
I - vu',
\]
a **rank-1 perturbation of the identity**. Its LU factors are in general **full** $(m{-}1)\times(m{-}1)$ matrices (both $L'$ and $U'$ are lower/upper triangular with $O(m^2)$ nonzero entries), so the total storage is $O(m^2)$.

**Why the permutation works.** The permutation moves the "arrowhead" (the dense first row $u'$ and first column $v$) to the **last** row and **last** column. This places the identity block $I$ in the **leading** position, so it is processed first by Gaussian elimination. Since $I$ is already triangular, no fill-in is generated in the bulk of the matrix; the only non-trivial work is confined to the single last row of $L$ (the vector $u$) and the single last column of $U$ (the vector $v$ plus the scalar pivot $1-u'v$). Thus the dense information, which was spread across an entire row and column ($O(m)$ each), remains $O(m)$ in the factors instead of proliferating into $O(m^2)$ fill-in.
